column1: # Expected values for `scripts/ctgrind.sh --check`. One row per CLAIM row of
# the table — i.e. per (module, optimize mode, harness target) measured with
# the secret TAINTED and the binary built WITH `-fvalgrind`.
# The control rows (untainted) and trap rows (no `-fvalgrind`) are not listed:
# the script requires 0 from every one of them unconditionally, since a
# non-zero there means the measurement itself is broken, never that the module
# changed.
# Deliberately NOT a diff of exact totals. `total` includes the harness's own
# non-constant-time hex formatter and whatever std internals it reaches, so it
# moves with a zig or valgrind upgrade for reasons that say nothing about the
# module — and a check that goes red for the wrong reason gets muted, which is
# worse than no check. `total_min` therefore only asserts that the propagation
# witness fired at all (a zero total would mean the taint never arrived, which
# would make every in-file zero meaningless).
# `in_file` accepts an exact count or a `>=N` / `<=N` bound:
#   exact  — the number a SPEC.md states as a fact about the module. Every
#            claimed zero is exact, and so are the two small non-zeros that
#            are documented line by line (ed448's three `Fe.invert`
#            validations; ecvrf's three try-and-increment branches on the
#            PUBLIC H).
#   bound  — counts a compiler or std change may legitimately move, where only
#            the direction is load-bearing: the ReleaseSafe
#            overflow-check flood that is chachapoly's positive control, and
#            std's `rejectIdentity` context that ct25519's negative control
#            needs only to EXIST.
# `out_sha` — the SEVENTH column, added 2026-09-08. A digest of the VALUE lines
# the harness itself printed on this row's claim run.
# ⛔ Why. The ct25519 audit (C1) mutated the HARNESS, not the module: the branch
# stopped calling `mulRistrettoBase` and assigned the secret straight to the
# output. The table came out identical to the baseline — 2 / 0 / 2 / 0 — and
# `--check` was GREEN. Every row claiming "in-file 0" has that hole, because a
# harness that never reaches the module also produces zero in-file contexts:
# "no secret-dependent branch" and "the module was not called" are the SAME
# measurement. That is 8 rows across 6 modules.
# What separates them is the value the harness prints, which every harness
# already did (`pk=`, `sig=`, `x=`, `create[N]=`, `cmov=`, `r=`/`s=`) — nothing
# needed a new print, only a pin. Verified on the deployed bypass: the counts
# stay 2/0/2/0 and pass, and ONLY this column fails.
# The two pins are complementary and neither subsumes the other. The source
# digest sees an edit to the analysed module; the output digest sees the harness
# failing to reach it. The bypass lives in the harness, which is not in any
# row's pattern, so the source digest does not move for it.
# Rewritten by `--update-outputs`, which RUNS the measurement (the value cannot
# come from anywhere else) — a separate verb from `--update-digests` for the
# same reason: re-pinning must be typed on purpose.
# Equal digests across rows are expected in two places and both are legitimate:
# chachapoly's two modes compute the same tag, and ct25519's two targets
# compute the same point by different routes. Each row still reads its OWN log
# (`log_<module>_<mode>_<vg>_<target>_<taint>.txt`), so no row can be scored on
# another's output.
# `src_sha` — the SIXTH column, added 2026-09-08. A 16-hex-digit sha256 over
# the module's OWN sources named by this row's `PATTERN`, concatenated in
# sorted order.
# ⛔ Why a source pin and not a location list. The k256 audit (G1) showed the
# in-file COUNT cannot see a leak that REPLACES an expected one, and proposed
# pinning `file:line` sets instead. Measured before building it: that does not
# work either. The reproduction substitutes `ecdsa_recover.zig:136` IN PLACE,
# so the file's numbering is unchanged and the stack line set is identical —
# and so is the error count (139 errors from 15 contexts, both runs). The two
# memcheck logs differ only in the pid. Nothing derived from the measurement
# separates them.
# So the pin is on the artefact: if the analysed sources change, the row goes
# red until someone re-reads the contexts and runs `--update-digests`. Coarse
# on purpose — a comment change trips it — because "the code that was analysed
# is the code that ships" is what the counts silently assumed.
# Verified on the deployed defect: with the substitution applied, every count
# check still passes (15/10/5/0, the baseline exactly) and ONLY the digest
# fails. Unmodified tree stays green. The defect deployed into each of the 43
# files these patterns name turns its own row red — no blind spots.
# `NO-OWN-SRC` means the pattern names no file of this module (ct25519/std
# points at std's sources). Such a row has no artefact pin and `--check` says
# so on every run rather than comparing two placeholders and passing.
# A NON-ZERO in_file is NOT automatically "fine". Every non-zero below is an
# accounted-for validation, itemised line by line in the owning module's
# SPEC.md — but the convention when one is NOT is to record it here anyway,
# marked DEFECT in the comment above the row. Recording a defect is deliberate:
# an unrecorded one is invisible, and a row that goes red when it is FIXED is
# how the fix gets noticed. That is exactly how the two montint rows below went
# from 7 and 5 to 0. Nobody should read a green `--check` as "every
# constant-time claim in this repo holds": it means "the measurements still say
# what they said when they were taken".
# Measured 2026-08-11 (chachapoly…ed448) and 2026-08-13 (k256, montint),
# zig 0.16.0, valgrind 3.26.0, x86_64 (i7-7920HQ), `poly1305.lanes = 4`. Change
# a number here only together with the module's SPEC.md table, and only after
# re-running the harness.
# module
# bolt8 — the module was outside this table until 2026-09-08 and its ledger
# recorded the constant-time verdict as "PASS (inherited)": read, never
# instrumented, while it holds the node's long-term static private key, the
# ephemeral keys, `temp_k*` and both transport keys (audit F10).
# ⚠ EVERY NON-ZERO BELOW IS NAMED, and none of them is a leak. In order:
#   dh 1        `q.rejectIdentity()` at the end of k256's constant-time ladder
#               (group.zig:278) -- a branch on "the product was the identity",
#               reachable only for k == 0 mod n. Same class k256's own table
#               already accounts for.
#   keygen 3    the invalid-secret rejections of `generateDeterministic`:
#               scalar canonicality (common.zig:75 via scalar.zig:87),
#               `if (d.isZero())` in bolt8's own dh.zig:80, and the same
#               `rejectIdentity` inside `combMulBaseWithTable` (group.zig:347).
#               All three reject a key that would be discarded anyway.
#   act3 6      2x std's `if (!verify)` tag check (chacha20.zig:713) -- branching
#               on the ANSWER is the API, and the comparison producing it is
#               std's constant-time one; plus 4 from decompressing the peer's
#               static key (group.zig:116/123/124, field.zig:162, sqrt at
#               field.zig:306) and one ECDH `mul`. `rs` is the peer's PUBLIC key,
#               but it arrives by decryption under a tainted key, so memcheck
#               cannot know that -- an artefact of the taint model, stated
#               rather than patched around.
#   transport 3 2x the same tag check, and `if (c.len != out.len + 16)` in
#               bolt8's transport.zig:149. The length came from `recvLength`,
#               i.e. from a decryption under a tainted key; a BOLT#8 message
#               length is a public property of the frame.
# `act1` has no row on purpose: the initiator's Act One never touches the static
# key, so its zero would say nothing about constant time. See the harness.

# The AEAD's own claim (added 2026-09-02). SPEC.md and root.zig state that the
# tag is compared in constant time, and until this row existed the module was
# measured with the `poly1305` target ALONE -- the harness never touched
# `root.zig`, so swapping `timing_safe.eql` for `std.mem.eql` left the whole
# suite green.
# ⚠ THE EXPECTED COUNT IS NOT ZERO, AND THE FOUR ARE NAMED. `in` for this
# target is `root.zig` PLUS std's `chacha20.zig`/`poly1305.zig`, because the
# module delegates every AEAD call at or below `aead_delegate_max` to std --
# their property is ours for those lengths, and attributing the contexts to
# std would be the same evasion as widening a pattern to make a count go away.
# At ReleaseFast the four are the ONE branch an AEAD cannot avoid, twice on
# each side of the delegation threshold: `if (!timing_safe.eql(computed, tag))`
# in `root.zig` (2) and the identical `if (!verify)` in std's `chacha20.zig`
# (2). Branching on the ANSWER is the API; the comparison that produced it is
# what has to be constant-time, and that is what the two `timing_safe.eql`
# calls are. A fifth context would mean a new branch on secret data.
# ReleaseSafe is `>=1` for the same reason the poly1305 row is: the
# lane-parallel MAC's checked arithmetic is reached through the AEAD too.
# ⛔ THE TWO DEBUG ROWS WERE REMOVED 2026-09-08, and the cause is now known.
# They were recorded here as KNOWN RED on 2026-09-02 -- valgrind printed the
# MAC's frames with no file:line at all
# (`poly1305.Generic(4).wide (in …/ctgrind-chachapoly)`), so no pattern could
# attribute them. On 2026-09-08 the SAME expectation passed on the same tree.
# The verdict was moving with the build, not with the module.
# Root cause: Zig 0.16 compiles Debug with the self-hosted x86_64 backend
# (the only mode where it is the default) and valgrind's DWARF reader cannot
# parse the `.debug_line` it emits -- 35 159 warnings on a ten-line program
# with no inline asm and no `std.valgrind` call, 0 for the same program built
# `-fllvm`, and the release modes break identically when forced `-fno-llvm`
# (48 395 / 37 369). Measured effect on attribution, same harness and target:
# ReleaseFast 36/36 frames carry `(file:line)`, ReleaseSafe 2054/2054, Debug
# 904/2130 -- and 51 of 60 resolved Debug frames carry the WRONG line.
# Not worked around with `-fllvm`, because the rows bought nothing: SPEC.md
# calls ReleaseSafe and Debug ONE positive control (210 and 281 contexts inside
# `poly1305.zig`, the same checked operators for the same reason), nothing here
# is consumed in Debug, and CONVENTIONS §7.1 narrowed the Debug CI lane to
# compile-only in 2026-08-15 on the same kind of measurement. See
# `scripts/ctgrind.sh` § MODES.
chachapoly
chachapoly

# material is routed ONLY through std's constant-time HMAC/AES-CCM, with no
# comparison or branch on key bytes in this module's own code; until today that
# sentence had no measurement behind it (audit F8).
# ⚠ THE TWO ZEROS ARE ZEROS WITH A WITNESS. An earlier probe reported `derive`
# and `protect` as 0 in-file out of a total of 0, which is not a result: a zero

# harness prints the derived keys and the ciphertext, so the totals are 4 and 2

# `unprotect` 1 is std's `if (!valid)` at aes_ccm.zig:152, AFTER the
# `crypto.timing_safe.eql` two lines above it. Branching on the answer is the
# API; the comparison that produced it is the constant-time one. It is here and
# not in the other two because only `unprotect` verifies a tag.

# k256 — the field layer is clean; every group/sign/ecdsa context is a
# `rejectIdentity`, an input/output validation, or (in `ecdsa` alone) the RFC
# 6979 §3.2 nonce-retry rejection, itemised line by line in
# `modules/k256/SPEC.md` and documented at the source in `ecdsa_recover.zig`.
# `ecdsa` was added 2026-08-13: `ecdsa_recover.sign` is a shipped secret path
# with an in-repo consumer (`lninvoice`) and had no target at all.
# ⛔⛔ hqc — THESE FOUR ROWS ARE A RECORDED DEFECT, not a clean claim, and they
# are the first ones in this file that are. The convention above says an
# unaccounted non-zero is recorded here anyway and marked DEFECT, because an
# unrecorded defect is invisible and a row that goes red when it is FIXED is
# how the fix gets noticed. This is that case — and on 2026-09-09 it did
# exactly that: the counts below were 52 / 26 / 33 and are now 14 / 4 / 6.
# The module's own docs said it has no secret-dependent branches because it
# structurally matches the reference. It does match — and the compiler undoes
# it. `writeSupportToVector` is a masked select with no `if` in the source;
# LLVM recognised the identity and rewrote it back into a branch that loads
# `bit_tab[k]` only on the taken path. Adjudicated in the disassembly as real
# `je`/`jne`/`jb`, not the known `cmov` false positive. That is now stopped by
# an `asm volatile ("" : "+r" (mask))` barrier in the inner loop — an opaque
# identity the compiler cannot see through, so it can no longer prove the
# select. THE BARRIER IS LOAD-BEARING: deleting it puts 38 contexts back, and
# these rows are what says so.
# WHAT THE FIX COST, measured before it was applied (min of 200 calls,
# ReleaseFast -Dcpu=native, three alternating runs per arm; the spread inside
# each arm was ≤1%, so the gap is far outside the noise):
#             without barrier   with barrier    delta
#   Re-derive with `modules/hqc/src/bench.zig` (opt in via HQC_BENCH=1); it was
#   written for this measurement. The trade taken: 38 secret-dependent branch
#   contexts out of the module's hottest secret path, for ~7% on a PQ KEM.
# Attribution, ReleaseFast, decaps (14) — `prng.zig:289`, which was 38 of the
# old 52, is GONE; everything below is what it always was:
#   gf256.zig:114   4   `if (s >= 255) s -= 255` — log-table reduction.
#   gf256.zig:113   3   `if (a == 0 or b == 0)` — GF(256) multiply short-circuit.
#   prng.zig:268    3   `if (found) support[idx] = …` — duplicate fixup.
#   reedsolomon     2   inlined, no line info (computeElp and encode).
#   prng.zig:216    1   `if (val < threshold) break` — rejection sampling.
#   prng.zig:223    1   `if (s == val) dup = true` — duplicate detection.
#   keygen (4): prng.zig:216 ×2, prng.zig:223 ×2 — the rejection loop only.
#   encaps (6): prng.zig:268 ×3, gf256.zig:114 ×2, reedsolomon ×1.
# `sampler` is 2, not 40, ON PURPOSE: that target drives the fixed-weight
# rejection sampler only (prng.zig:216 and :223) and never reaches the scatter,
# which runs later when the support is turned into a bit vector. It isolates
# the loop so a change there is attributable; it is not a smaller measurement
# of the same thing. It is unchanged by the barrier, which is the expected
# result and a small check that the drop elsewhere is the scatter and not a
# measurement artefact.
# ⚠ The count is STILL WORSE in the mode a cautious consumer deploys, and the
# barrier does not fix that: measured on decaps, ReleaseFast 14, **ReleaseSafe
# 92** (was 130). The remaining ~78 are the overflow checks in
# reedmuller.decodeSymbol becoming branches on secret-derived data — a
# different defect in the same module, untouched by this fix. Only ReleaseFast
# is pinned; a second mode doubles the rows for a claim of the same shape, and
# Debug cannot be measured at all.
# ⚠ HONEST BOUND: memcheck says "Conditional jump OR MOVE". These were
# adjudicated as real jumps. Whether a key is practically extractable from them
# was NOT measured; that is different and much more expensive work. The claim
# is "the module's stated property does not hold and nothing was testing it",
# not "the key is out".
# hqc, 2026-09-09. decaps 14 -> 2, encaps 6 -> 0. FOUR fixes, all measured:
#   gf256.mul/inverse   dropped the exp/log tables -- the only secret-INDEXED
#                       table loads verified anywhere in this repo (+7.3% decaps)
#   sampleFixedWeightBiased   duplicate fixup blends under a mask
#   maskNonzero               laundered; LLVM had turned the branch-free
#                             `x != 0` trick back into a branch
#   Berlekamp-Massey mask12   same, one barrier covers the whole update
# The last three cost nothing measurable; the 7.3% is the algorithm swap alone.
# ⭐ Everything left, in EVERY target, is `sampleFixedWeightRejection`
# (prng.zig:216 the rejection loop, :223 the accept decision). Spec v5.0.0 §3.5
# REQUIRES that sampler for keygen's x/y, and decaps re-derives y from the seed
# on every call because the spec fixes a seed-sized dkKEM. ⛔ Do NOT mask :223 to
# make this number smaller: the leak is the ENCLOSING loop's trip count, so the
# context would go and the timing signal would stay -- a prettier measurement of
# the same defect. See SPEC.md.
# ⭐ encaps' 0 means something only because the row carries an output pin.

# aescbc — the two padding strippers, the only place this module does its own
# arithmetic over a secret. ⭐ The claim these rows test is NOT "zero": both
# functions END in `if (invalid != 0) return error.InvalidPadding` and return

# own words forbid is an EARLY EXIT from the scan or a distinct signal per
# failure reason, and the scan loop contributes 0 contexts, so there is neither.

# ── sealedbox: the secret-key text codecs ──────────────────────────────────
# ⭐ These four were 8 / 7 / 43 / 47 until 2026-09-09, all of it std's
# table-driven base64 and hex reached with a SECRET argument: 95 of the 105
# contexts were reported on a LOAD, and the disassembly showed
# `movzbl <table>(%reg)` over a secret byte and over a secret 6-bit group --
# the cache-timing class of T-table AES. The module now carries its own
# table-free codecs for SECRET material only; the public-key codecs still use
# std, deliberately, because their input discloses nothing.
# The ENCODERS are pinned at exact 0: they are pure arithmetic, and the only
# indexed load left in the disassembly is `key[i]` over the loop counter.
# ⛔ The PARSERS are pinned at 1 and a 0 there would be WRONG. The remaining
# context is `if (invalid != 0)` -- the accept/reject decision the function
# returns to its caller anyway, same reasoning as aescbc above. What the
# constant-time claim forbids is an early exit that reveals WHICH character
# was bad, and the decode loops contribute 0 contexts, so there is none.
# ⭐⭐ The out_sha values did not move by a single bit across the fix: the
# branch changed, the result did not.
# ⚠ Measured, not reviewed -- and the reason is on this very module. The first
# draft of `ctEq` put the optimisation barrier on the INPUT, which hides the
# value but not the structure; LLVM still turned `ctEq(c,'+') & 62` into a
# `test`/`je` at `root.zig:292`. Only moving the barrier onto the resulting
# MASK removed it. Source review would not have found that.
# ⛔⛔ AND THE COUNTS ALONE WOULD NOT HOLD THIS. Verified by deploying the
# defect: with `blackBox` deleted from `ctEq`/`ctGe`, only `b64dec` moves
# (1 -> 5). `hexenc`, `hexdec` and `b64enc` keep their exact counts and are
# caught ONLY by the src_sha column. So on three of these four rows the source
# pin is the whole gate, which is why the guard-stripping fix that gave bolt3
# its pin back matters here too -- a row with NO-OWN-SRC and an unchanged count
# would have let the barrier be deleted in silence.

# ── pir: the query index, and the client's check ───────────────────────────
# A1 `pir.md` M2 -- the module's central claim had never been machine-checked,
# and its sibling `fss` exposed a REAL defect the day it entered the gate.
# ⛔ Both rows are pinned at 1 and a 0 would be WRONG on both.
#  * `query` 1 = `pir.zig:146` `if (index >= domain_size)`, a contract check on
#    a PUBLIC bound whose outcome the caller already knows (it chose the index).
#  * `reconstruct` 1 = `verify.zig:453` `if (diff != 0) return AnswerRejected`,
#    which SPEC.md calls "the protocol's own public output" -- the abort is
#    visible by definition.
# What the claim forbids is a branch revealing WHICH word mismatched, and the
# fixed-trip loops contribute 0. That is the SPEC sentence, measured.
# ⚠ The PRG is pinned to Sha256Prg, NOT the default Aes128Mmo, whose
# `constant_time` is `aes.has_hardware_support`. On an AES-NI host the default
# would measure green for a reason that does not hold on a soft-AES host, and
# SPEC.md says the soft fallback leaks the query index. A row whose colour
# depends on the gate's CPU says nothing. ⛔ So a green `query` row is NOT a
# claim about the default instantiation on a soft-AES target.
